title: introduce-slo-umbrella-and-circuit-snooze-hotfix
author: Ava Thompson
release_notes: Introduce an SLO umbrella controller to coordinate temporary SLO relaxations across affected tenants during transient regional pressure; add 'circuit-snooze' to prevent flip-flopping circuits while KV-sync stabilizes; telemetry for snooze windows and umbrella decisions.
description:
Context and motivation: In production incident SUP-4821 we observed repeated circuit reopen/reclose oscillations during KV-sync jitter and transient region saturation. Those flips caused cascading tenant churn and made automated failovers amplify load instead of absorbing it. This PR introduces two coordinated pieces: (1) an SLO Umbrella controller that can apply short-lived, controlled SLO relaxations grouped by region/cohort to reduce admission pressure and allow graceful routing fallbacks; (2) a Circuit Snooze mechanism that temporarily freezes circuit state transitions for a configurable window when KV-sync variance or bursty telemetry is detected. Both are designed to be conservative defaults (short windows, telemetry-driven) and fully overridable by operator policies.

Summary of changes / checklist: - Add slo_umbrella controller in control-plane/slo (controller, API handlers, unit tests). - Add circuit_snooze logic inside runtime/circuit (state machine pause + metrics). - Add KV-sync jitter detector (runtime/kv/jitter_detector) and hook into snooze decision. - Wire a new admin flag: controlplane.slo_umbrella.enabled (default true) and runtime.circuit_snooze.window_ms (default 1500). - Export new telemetry: slo_umbrella.decisions, circuit_snooze.activations, kv.jitter_score. - Add e2e scenario to perf-canary (simulated regional saturation + kv jitter). - Hotfix: change to kv-sync backoff logic to avoid immediate reopen on out-of-order ACKs.

Implementation notes and rationale: The SLO Umbrella is implemented as a best-effort coordinator: it observes per-tenant SLO breach risk signals and issues ephemeral 'umbrella' tokens that the serving edge uses to (a) temporarily widen latency targets for low-priority routes, and (b) prefer local cached responses or smaller model variants. The umbrella token TTLs are small (default 5s) and issuance is rate-limited per-region. Circuit Snooze takes a conservative approach: when jitter_detector detects > threshold variance in KV sync latency or missing heartbeat bursts, it transitions the circuit state machine to an "aligned" pause state where reopen attempts are suppressed for window_ms. Snoozes are recorded in telemetry and count toward failure budgets so behavior is auditable.

Testing and CI: - Unit tests: added for controller and snooze machine (coverage + boundary cases). - Integration: local integration run against mini-cluster passes. - Perf-canary: new scenario added and validated in staging (simulated kv jitter + regional saturation). - CI: build & lint & unit tests passed on first run; flaky e2e in earlier iteration fixed by reducing default TTLs.

I'm worried about masking real SLO degradation for too long." - Ava: "Agreed; reduced default from 10s to 5s and added rate-limits per-region. Added telemetry to show duration distribution." - Diego: "Snooze looks good but needs a circuit-level audit event for every transition." - Ava: "Added audit events and a lightweight trace span for snooze activations." - Liam: "What's the operator story to opt out?" - Ava: "controlplane.slo_umbrella.enabled=false and runtime flag runtime.circuit_snooze.enabled=false; documented in ops guide." - Diego (approval): "LGTM pending one nit on metric name; approved after rename." - Riya (approval): "Approved. Verified staging canary metrics show reduced reopen churn."
